summary: Ran targeted backend + frontend regression for supplier GHG Logs duplicate-visibility fix. Verified /api/emissions for supplier hides superseded revisions, helper logic covers legacy non-lineage rows, and MongoDB still retains historical records for the reported relationship.
action_items: Optional: provide valid credentials for goyalsomil+27@hotmail.com if direct user-reported account reproduction is required.
Optional maintainability follow-up: split oversized frontend file /app/frontend/src/pages/Emissions.js (>700 lines) into smaller modules/components.
critical_code_review_comments: GET /api/emissions applies exclude_reopened_supplier_submission_revisions() before response serialization, matching intended dedupe path.
exclude_reopened_supplier_submission_revisions now filters supplier rows where is_current_revision is explicitly false, which covers legacy rows missing revision_lineage_id.
Emissions.js is very large (3454 lines), exceeding maintainability guideline threshold and increasing regression risk.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Supplier UI checked on /ghg/scope1 with data-testid row selectors (2 visible rows, no duplicate rendering observed). Live backend test confirms /api/emissions returns no supplier rows with is_current_revision=false for supplier account goyalsomil+919@hotmail.com. MongoDB check confirms reported relationship 53d631c3-9bc7-4c20-babc-068bc53af68f still contains both current and historical (is_current_revision=false) records, so audit history is retained.
rca of the issue: Original duplication came from old submitted rows remaining visible after unlock/resubmission. Those historical rows were marked is_current_revision:false but some lacked revision_lineage_id, so prior lineage-based filtering missed them. New filtering by source=supplier + is_current_revision=false removes superseded rows from normal GHG Logs while preserving records in MongoDB for audit/revision history.
